similarities.point: Both identify the deities as gods of Samothrace.
similarities.quote_britannica: being a name given to the gods of Samotbracia
similarities.quote_wikipedia: centered in the north Aegean Islands of Lemnos and possibly Samothrace

similarities.point: Both state the deities were worshipped in other parts of Greece.
similarities.quote_britannica: They were allo worthipped in other parts of Greece, as Lemos and Thehees
similarities.quote_wikipedia: The Cabeiri were also worshipped at other sites in the vicinity

similarities.point: Both mention the number four in connection with the gods.
similarities.quote_britannica: the fests go are laid to be, in number, four, viz. Axieros, Axiocerla, Axiocerfius, and Calinila
similarities.quote_wikipedia: usually between two and four, some of either sex

similarities.point: Both list Axieros as one of the deities.
similarities.quote_britannica: the fests go are laid to be, in number, four, viz. Axieros, Axiocerla, Axiocerfius, and Calinila
similarities.quote_wikipedia: Axierus and Axiocersa for the pair of females

differences.point: Britannica calls them gods of the ancient Pagars; Wikipedia calls them enigmatic chthonic deities.
differences.quote_britannica: a term in the biology of the ancient Pagars, figuring great and powerful gods
differences.quote_wikipedia: were a group of enigmatic chthonic deities

differences.point: Britannica names four specific gods; Wikipedia says the number varies and lists different common names.
differences.quote_britannica: the fests go are laid to be, in number, four, viz. Axieros, Axiocerla, Axiocerfius, and Calinila
differences.quote_wikipedia: The number of Cabeiri also varies, with some accounts citing four (often a pair of males and a pair of females)

differences.point: Britannica mentions festivals called cabinets; Wikipedia describes a nine-day festival with extinguished fires.
differences.quote_britannica: where the cabinets were celebrated in honour of them
differences.quote_wikipedia: Lemnos held an annual festival of the Cabeiri, lasting nine days, during which all the fires were extinguished

differences.point: Britannica gives no etymology; Wikipedia discusses Semitic, Hittite, and pre-Greek origins.
differences.quote_britannica: CABIRI, a term in the biology of the ancient Pagars
differences.quote_wikipedia: In the past, the Semitic word kabir ("great") has been compared to Κάβειροι since at least Joseph Justus Scaliger
